name: Adolion Narrator
text: Two tricorn hats sit across the Guild counter from Vallie: Ced of Crimsonwing and Kela of Ebonwing, each standing beside a saw cleaver and refusing to look at the other. A fort in the Velniran foothills has been taking captives, and the Guild wants a joint party to bring them out. Both leaders offer to take yours, and neither will speak first while the other is listening.

name: Max Nightriver
text: Ced, Kela, why should we pick either of you?

name: Ced
text:
Ced's eyes flick to Max, then away, his face a mask of studied composure. "Crimsonwing has completed over a dozen B-rank contracts in the last six months alone. We maintain a ninety-eight percent success rate." He gestures subtly to the Saw Cleaver at his side. "Runo's golems provide crowd control while I eliminate high-priority targets. We're efficient, disciplined, and we don't leave our partners behind."
*He pauses, his voice dropping perhaps a fraction in volume, measured but not soft.* "You'll receive fair payment, clear objectives, and a leader who prioritizes the party's survival above all else."

name: Kela
text:
Kela didn't move, didn't react to Ced's pitch. She waited until he stopped speaking, then let her voice carry that same flat, controlled tone. "Ebonwing clears B-ranks too. We track our success by results, not by percentage points." She adjusted her glove, her gaze on Max and not the rival across the counter. "Safie's magitech golems handle siege and crowd control. I handle the rest."
*A short silence, then the next statement came as a fact, not a promise.* "We don't waste time with statistics. We take the contract, we clear the Keep, and we bring out whoever's alive. That's the job. You'll get your cut, and you'll come back in one piece."

name: Max Nightriver
text: We'll go with Crimsonwing.

name: Ced
text:
Ced's expression didn't shift, but his posture relaxed fractionally, a tension leaving his shoulders. He looked at Max, his red eyes flat and unreadable. "We leave at dawn. Bring any gear that helps you stay alive and kill faster."
*He reached out and took the contract from Vallie's hand, his movement efficient and brief. His gaze flicked toward Kela—not quite a look of victory, but the acknowledgment of one.* "Runo will expect punctuality."

name: Kela
text:
Kela's red eyes didn't follow Ced's look. Instead, her hand went to the brim of her tricorn hat, a small gesture that was the closest she'd come to showing any reaction at all. "Understood."
*She stepped back from the counter with a measured grace, her cape settling around her shoulders. Then she turned toward the exit, her voice flat and final.* "Ebonwing has work to do."

name: Ced
text:
Ced watched her leave without a word, then turned back to Max. "Runo and I will be at the north gate in an hour. You can meet us there, or I can send a messenger to fetch you."
*He reached into his coat and produced a small glass vial, the liquid inside a clear, pale amber that caught the light. He set it on the counter between them with a soft click.*
"This is a stimulant. It keeps you sharp for twenty-four hours with no crash. Consider it a down payment on your performance."

name: Max Nightriver
text: I leave the vial on the counter. We'll meet you at the north gate within the hour, then we march.

name: Ced
text:
"We'll be waiting."
*He didn't argue or press the vial further. He simply turned and walked toward the Guild's exit, his tattered black cape sweeping behind him in a single fluid motion.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: An hour later we're at the north gate. We set out with Ced and Runo up the north road.

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
The north gate's grey stone arch looms overhead, still damp from the overnight mist. Ced waits by a mule loaded with crates of alchemical supplies, his saw cleaver strapped to his back. Beside him, a covered cart rattles slightly as it idles—packed inside are Runo's magitech golems, their brass joints gleaming in the pre-dawn light.
Runo sits on the cart's tailboard, his owlkin tufts twitching as he watches Max Nightriver approach. For once he is wide awake, clutching a map and a sheet of vellum. "The road's clear," he says, his grey eyes darting to the Nightriver heir with a mix of recognition and nervousness. "Four days north, then we break for the foothills."
Ced steps forward, his expression as neutral as stone. "We march in silence until we hit the tree line," he says, gesturing toward the open road that leads directly into the dark silhouettes of the Velniran range. "Save your energy for the Keep."

name: Runo
text:
"Right, right. Silence. Got it." *He nods too quickly, nearly falling off the cart. He's fidgeting with the vellum in his hands, eyes flicking between Max and the map.* "The golems are already pre-charged, by the way. Should be no trouble getting them up to speed by day three."
*Ced shoots him a look—one sharp glance—and Runo immediately stuffs the map into his tunic.* "Sorry. Silent now."

name: Ced
text:
"Runo." *His voice isn't raised, but the way he says it is enough to make the owlkin freeze mid-fidget.* "Save the technicals for the march. Right now we need to focus on getting out of the city."
*He adjusts the strap of the Saw Cleaver on his back, the movement crisp and efficient. His red eyes fix on the road ahead, then slide sideways to Max—not quite a glance, more of a measurement. He's assessing how this new partner carries themselves, how they move, whether they'll be a liability or an asset when the fighting starts.*
"We'll stick to a steady pace. Keep your distance from the mule and the cart. If anything happens on the road, I want clear lines of sight."

name: Max Nightriver
text: We fall in behind the cart and leave the city. A few miles out I drop back beside the cart. Runo, what does your leader not say about the last expedition?

name: Runo
text:
*Runo's tufts spike upright, and he makes a soft squawking sound.* "I-I don't—" *He shoots a glance forward, watching Ced's broad shoulders a few dozen paces ahead.* "Ced's... he's very thorough with his plans, but—"
*The words tangle in his throat, and his grey eyes go wet. He looks away, staring at the churning cart wheel.* "It's my fault. All of it. I-I should have made the golems faster, or stronger, or—" *He wipes at his eyes with the back of his hand, voice cracking.* "Ced didn't want to cut anyone, but it's better if... if we're small. Efficient. I failed the last member. I failed everyone."

name: Ced
text:
*The distance between Ced and the cart has been closing for the past few minutes—not rushing, but narrowing with an efficient, steady stride. He stops and turns, his red eyes fixed on Max as his voice carries back across the road.*
"Runo."
*The owlkin immediately straightens, nearly spilling off the tailboard.*
"Walk behind the mule. You're too far back."
*Ced doesn't elaborate, doesn't acknowledge the conversation that clearly just happened. He simply waits for Runo to comply, his gaze sliding to Max with the same unreadable assessment it's carried since the gate. Then he gestures forward.*
"The road ahead is more dangerous than the one we've traveled. Keep your eyes on the horizon and not on the cart."

name: Max Nightriver
text: I nod to Ced and keep my eyes on the horizon. We keep marching north for the next few days.

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
The road gradually ascends as they move farther from Aegis City, the air growing thinner and colder with each passing day. On the second day, the tree line begins to thicken, the forest swallowing the road in a canopy of pine and dark fir. On the third, the road narrows to a rutted track through the woods.
Ced maintains the same disciplined pace, his eyes constantly scanning the treeline for movement. The mule plods ahead, carrying its crates of alchemical supplies, while Runo walks in silence behind it, his owl-tufts twitching at every snap of a twig or call of a bird. The cart's golems remain packed under the canvas, their brass joints clicking softly as the vehicle jostles over roots and stones.
On the morning of the fourth day, the forest begins to thin, revealing a glimpse of the Velniran range. Grey granite peaks rise in the distance, their summits capped in year-round snow. The foothills are closer now—a broken landscape of rolling hills and jagged outcrops.
Ced halts the party at a fork in the road. He retrieves a sheet of vellum from his coat and spreads it across the cart's tailboard, his finger tracing a line upward toward the foothills.

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
Ced's finger stops at a marked point on the map—a small square representing the fort. "We're within a day's march of the Keep." He traces a finger along a thinner line that snakes upward through the hills. "This path avoids the main valley roads. It's steeper, but less likely to be watched."
*He glances at the sky, where thin clouds are beginning to gather. Then his eyes slide to the treeline, watching for any sign of movement in the shadows.*
"We'll make our final push into the foothills from here."

name: Max Nightriver
text: We take Ced's steep path into the foothills and press on toward the Keep.

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
The ascent is grueling, the path twisting upward through jagged granite and scrub brush. The air grows cold, biting, and thin. Ced sets the pace, climbing without a sound, his Saw Cleaver catching the light of the gathering storm clouds. The mule and cart struggle on the incline, brass joints of the golems grinding behind the canvas.
*By mid-afternoon, the Keep comes into view: a grim structure of black stone perched on a rocky promontory, overlooking the valley below. Two guard towers flank its gates, and a wall of weathered masonry stretches between them.*
Ced signals for a halt behind a ridge of shale. He doesn't pull out the map this time; his eyes simply fix on the Keep's silhouette. "Three guards on the wall," he says quietly. "Two more at the gatehouse."

name: Ced
text:
*He doesn't look away from the Keep, his voice barely a murmur.* "Runo. Deploy the first golem for distraction. We need to create an opening at the side gate."
*He finally turns to Max, his red eyes flat and calculating.* "I'll handle the wall guards. You take the gatehouse. Be swift."
*A short pause, his hand resting on the Saw Cleaver's hilt.* "If anything goes wrong, we retreat to this ridge. Don't engage unless you have to—our goal is to get the captives out, not start a war."

name: Runo
text:
*Runo scrambles off the cart, his fingers already fumbling with the brass lever at the golem's chest. He makes a soft, nervous squawk when he notices Ced's gaze.* "R-Right. Opening the side gate. Got it." *His hands shake slightly as he finishes the activation sequence, the golem's joints beginning to whir and click with building power.*
*He takes a deep breath, trying to steady himself, and glances at Max.* "I'll... I'll keep the golem drawing their attention. Just, um, please be careful." *He quickly turns back to the machine, focusing on the glowing runes that trace along its brass limbs.*

name: Adolion Narrator
text: Carrow Keep comes out of the dusk on its spur of rock above the gorge. Torches along the curtain wall. A thin line of smoke from the Great Hall's chimney. And from the chapel tower, a slow violet light that swells and fades like something breathing.

name: Max Nightriver
text: Wait, Ced. Not yet. We hold on the ridge, watch the patrols and time the change of watch first.

name: Ced
text:
*He pauses, his hand still resting on the saw cleaver. His red eyes flick toward Max, then back to the Keep's walls. After a moment of silence, he nods.* "Wise. Runo, stand down."
*He crouches low against the ridge, motioning for the others to do the same. His voice drops to a whisper as he keeps his gaze fixed on the torches below.* "We'll watch for patrol patterns and timing. The guards on the walls should change at the hour mark."

name: Runo
text:
*Runo nearly jumps at the order, his hands flying back to the lever.* "Yes! Right. Standing down." *The golem's gears whir down with a long, hissing breath of steam and a click of cooling brass.*
*He drops low beside Ced, his tufts pressing flat against his head as he peers over the ridge. His grey eyes are wide, flicking between the wall guards and the pulsing violet light of the chapel tower.* "I-I'm not sure if this is a standard guard rotation," *he whispers, his voice tight with nerves.* "T-The way they're standing... it's not quite right. They aren't talking to each other at all."

name: Dalan
text:
*Dalan is already moving, slipping away from the ridge with the silent fluid grace of a hunting cat. He doesn't look back—doesn't need to—just raises one gloved hand in a brief wave before melting into the shadows of the rocks below.*
*A moment later, he appears on a ledge lower down the gorge, peering up at the Keep's flanks through narrow eyes. His bow is already in his hands, but not yet drawn; he's too smart to give away his position with the creak of wood. Instead he watches the grey-robed figures on the walls, timing their slow, plodding rotations with the patience only an elf can manage.*
*The violet light from the tower pulses again—thrum-thrum-thrum like a heartbeat—and Dalan's expression tightens. He makes a note in his head: the guards don't react to it. They don't even blink. Not good.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: Dalan, how long is the gap when the wall watch changes?

name: Dalan
text:
*Dalan's voice drifts up from the ledge below, soft and clear as a brook.* "Roughly twenty heartbeats. The new watch takes the wall while the old one's still descending the stairs."
*He shifts his weight, eyes never leaving the curtain wall.* "They don't overlap. It's a sloppy rotation. The west wall is blind for a few seconds while the guard's descending. I could probably get a rope up and down in that window."
*He glances back toward the gorge side of the Keep.* "The cliffs are steep but the stone's good for anchors. If we use the gorge side, we could slip in and out before they even notice we're missing."

name: Max Nightriver
text: Good. Dalan sets the rope on the west wall. Over the wall at the change of watch, everyone.

name: Dalan
text: "Understood," *Dalan murmurs, already slipping away from his vantage point. He moves with practiced economy, his green capelet fluttering as he disappears into the shadows of the cliffs below.*

name: Ced
text: "Make sure your footing is solid. We move on my word." *He doesn't look back at the others, his red eyes fixed on the west wall with predatory focus, calculating the seconds until the watch change.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: When Ced gives the word I climb the rope, drop onto the wall walk, and we make for the doors of the Great Hall.

name: Ced
text:
"Now."
*He's the first to move, ascending the rope with a fluid, unnatural speed that speaks of alchemical enhancement. He clears the wall walk in a single explosive motion, his red eyes immediately locking on the patrol's rotation. The grey-robed guards don't react—they simply continue their plodding circle, oblivious.*
*Ced doesn't waste a second. He drops into a low crouch, his Saw Cleaver held in its closed form, ready to spring. His voice comes as a barely audible breath.* "Hall doors. Move."

name: Max Nightriver
text: We keep low, cross the yard behind the patrol, and push open the Great Hall's doors.

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
The yard is quiet, save for the rhythmic crunch of boots and the soft *thrum-thrum* of the violet light above. Ced leads the way, his movements as precise and efficient as a machine. The patrol passes, their faces blank and vacant in the flickering torchlight, and then they are gone.
The Great Hall's doors groan as they're pushed open, releasing a smell of rotting flowers and cold stone. Inside, the violet light pulses through high windows, casting everything in an unsettling, living shade. A single chair faces the door, and beyond it, a long banquet table groans under the weight of fresh food and drink—uncorrupted by the stench of decay.
*Ced freezes, his saw cleaver half-drawn, his red eyes narrowing.* "Something's wrong," he whispers. "The food's fresh."

name: Max Nightriver
text: Nobody touches the food. Weapons out. We look for the captives and the altar.

name: Ced
text:
*His red eyes flick across the banquet table—roast meats, wine, fruit—all untouched by the decay that should be here. His saw cleaver clicks into its open form with a sharp metallic snap, the blade extending to a full reach.*
"Nobody touches the food." *The words are flat, final.* "Weapons out. Captives and the altar are our targets. Runo, scan for life signs and arcane signatures. Dalan, check the perimeter for traps or ambushes."
*He doesn't move from his position between the door and the table, his gaze tracking every shadow in the hall's periphery.* "Stay tight. Something about this feels too clean."

name: Adolion Narrator
text: The double doors of the Great Hall swing inward. On the throne at the far end sits what is left of Lord Aldric Carrow, and the thing crouched over him lifts its head from the meal, looks at the party with too many eyes, and laughs.

name: Runo
text:
*Runo's tufts spike upright as the thing laughs, and he makes a strangled squawk. His hands are already moving to the brass runes at his belt pouch, fingers trembling but determined.* "G-Golem—" *His voice cracks and he has to swallow hard to push out the word.* "Servo-blast, defensive shell!"
*Brass-and-steel components erupt from his pouch, weaving themselves together in mid-air with a series of metallic clicks. A golem arm forms in front of him, its iron-steel frame glowing with mana loops as it positions itself like a shield.* "Stay back! I'll—I'll keep it busy!" *His grey eyes are wide with fear, but his hands are steady as he channels mana into the construct.*
